  How to Submit Public Comment:

  Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
  methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

  In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
  Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
  Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

  Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website or by email as noted
  below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would
  disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read.
  Your comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

  1. Website: Please submit your comments using our online public comment form at Public Comment.

  2. Email: Please submit your comments via email to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on
  the subject line of your email: PUBLIC COMMENT: 04/04/2023 Regular Meeting.

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, April 4, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Harrington
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF FIRE DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEES

  •  FIRE ENGINEER JORDAN MILLER
  •  FIRE CAPTAIN CHRISTOPHER FETNER
  •  FIRE DIVISION CHIEF DOUGLAS SHONKWILER

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular March 7, 2023 Regular Meeting.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular March 21, 2023 Regular Meeting.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 4, 2023  2
   The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. MAYOR’S APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES -
  COUNCIL LIAISONS

  The Mayor is responsible for appointing members of the City Council to serve
  on various local and regional committees, as well as liaisons for City initiatives.
  In addition, it is necessary for the Council to take formal action to designate the
  new Mayor to serve as the Delegate to the Los Angeles County Sanitation
  District Board and Los Angeles County City Selection Committee. There is no
  fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-18 confirming
  the Mayor’s appointments of Council Members to serve as delegates, alternates
  and liaisons to outside agencies and Committees.

  D. REQUEST TO APPROVE COMMUNITY PARTNER AGREEMENT IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $8,500 WITH KABOOM!, INCORPORATED FOR COOLIDGE
  SCHOOL PARK

  Coolidge School Park is part of a joint-use agreement between the City and San
  Gabriel Unified School District. Through a grant application process, the park is
  being considered for a new playground with KABOOM!, Incorporated. In order
  to proceed to the next phase and be considered for funding, both the City and
  the San Gabriel Unified School District are being asked to sign a Community
  Partner Agreement with KABOOM!, Inc. The financial commitment to the
  partnership is $8,500 to cover a small percentage toward the purchase of the
  playground equipment. Since this is a joint-use park and project, the City

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 4, 2023  3
   proposes to cover half the cost of the required amount, which is $4,250. These
  funds will be paid out of budgeted general fund dollars in the Community
  Services Department. San Gabriel Unified School District will cover the other
  half of the cost.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review the Community Partner
  Agreement and authorize the City Manager to sign the Agreement and act as
  the agent of the City on all matter concerning this project.

  E. GENERAL PLAN HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT FOR
  THE 2022 CALENDAR YEAR

  Under the provisions of Government Code Section 65400(b), the Planning
  Division is required to provide an annual report to the California Department
  of Housing and Community Development and to the Governor’s Office of
  Planning and Research regarding the implementation of the General Plan’s
  Housing Element and how the City is meeting the regional housing needs for
  the community. The General Plan Annual Progress Report is an important tool
  to facilitate the implementation of the Housing Element and to assist in tracking
  and monitoring the City’s progress in addressing the Regional Housing Needs
  Allocation, including the number of housing units permitted by income level,
  the status of programs in the Housing Element, and efforts to remove
  governmental constraints. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the information
  contained in the staff report and direct staff to submit the housing report to
  the State Department of Housing and Community Development.

  F. 2022 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:
  JANUARY 2022 – DECEMBER 2022

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 4, 2023  4
   Under provisions of Government Code Section 65400(a)(2), the City is required
  to provide an annual report each April to the City Council, and the State
  Governor’s Office of Planning and Research regarding the status of the General
  Plan and its implementation progress. The Planning Commission reviewed the
  information at their March 13, 2023 meeting, affirmed the information in the
  report and recommended it be forwarded to the City Council. There is no fiscal
  impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the information
  contained in the staff report and direct staff to submit the report to the Office
  of Planning and Research and State Department of Housing and Community
  Development.

  G. ADOPTING RESOLUTION NO. 23-12 APPROVING THE SIDE LETTER OF
  AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE MANAGEMENT GROUP

  Representatives of the City and San Gabriel Police Management Group have
  agreed to amend the standing Memorandum of Understanding to clarify the
  vacation leave accrual rate credit provided to lateral hires, incorporate the
  requirements of State Assembly Bill 1949 (AB 1949) into the bereavement leave
  position, and establish a new special supervisor pay assignment for the
  Community Engagement Bureau. The new CEB special supervisor pay
  assignment will provide a $300 monthly stipend to the employee assigned to
  supervise the unit and have a total annualized cost impact of $3,600. There will
  be no net cost impact for Fiscal Year 2022-23 because the department
  transferred the special supervisor’s pay assignment from the Recruitment and
  Training Bureau to the CEB as part of its restructuring.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 4, 2023  5
   1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-12, which approves the Side Letter of Agreement
  amending the standing Memorandum of Understanding between the City
  and Police Management Group; and
  2. Authorize the City’s negotiators to execute the Side Letter of Agreement.

  H. NEW NATIONAL OPIOIDS SETTLEMENTS: TEVA, ALLERGAN, CVS,
  WALGREENS, AND WALMART AND STATUS UPDATE REGARDING
  PREVIOUS OPIOID DISTRIBUTOR AND JANSEN SETTLEMENT
  AGREEMENTS

  The City has previously approved Resolution No. 21-60 which authorized staff
  to participate in an Opioid Distributor Settlement Agreement. There have been
  recent updates concerning the payment amounts the City will receive and new
  Settlement Agreements with Opioid Distributors that the City may consider
  entering into. This is an update regarding recent discussions with the
  settlement administrators concerning payment amounts and the City’s option
  to enter into the new national opioid distributor settlements before the
  deadline of April 18, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Attorney to execute
  the necessary settlement and participation agreements for the new national
  opioid settlements that have been reached with Teva, Allergen, CVS, Walgreens,
  and Walmart.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. DIRECTION  ON  THE  TEMPORARY  OUTDOOR  BUSINESS  PERMIT
  PROGRAM

  The City’s Temporary Outdoor Business Permit Program (Program) was
  established on July 21, 2020, to allow for the temporary permitting of outdoor
  business areas, and/or drive-up or curbside pick-up or take-out designated
  parking areas, to assist businesses in safely accommodating for customers while

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 4, 2023  6
   adhering to the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health protocols for
  social distancing and health considerations related to the COVID-19 pandemic.
  Recently, on February 28, 2023, the state of emergency declared by Governor
  Newsom in response to the COVID-19 pandemic expired. Staff is seeking
  direction from the City Council on the Temporary Outdoor Business Permit
  Program now that the state of emergency has ended. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council provide direction on the Temporary
  Outdoor Business Permit Program (Program) and whether to continue the
  existing Program, continue the Program with staff-recommended modifications
  or discontinue the Program.

  B. PUBLIC WORKS ANNUAL UPDATE

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, April 18, 2023 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF APRIL 4, 2023
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:32 P.M. on Tuesday, April 4, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South M ission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Harrington.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Publ ic Works

I  Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven
  Wallace, Human Resources/Risk Management Director
  Edward Macias, Finance Director William Kaholokula,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes,
  Acting Police Chief Rikimaru Nakamura, Assistant City
  Clerk Marilyn Bonus, and Community Services Manager
  Matthew Morales-Stevens.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Special City Council Meeting of April 4, 2023:

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6)

  City Negotiators - City Manager Lazzaretto, City Attorney Lemieux, and Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Macias

  Regarding the following Employee Organizations - San Gabriel Police Officers'
  Association, San Gabriel Police Management Group, San Gabriel Firefighters'

I  Association, San Gabriel Fire Management Group and all Unrepresented
  Employees.

  City Attorney Lemieux announced that there was no reportable action.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 6  April 4, 2023
   1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved .

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF FIRE DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEES

  •  FIRE ENGINEER JORDAN MILLER

I  •  FIRE DIVISION CHIEF DOUGLAS SHONKWILER

  The presentation was made by Fire Chief Wallace and a ceremonial Oath of Office
  was administered by Chief City Clerk Clark.

  B. RECOGNITION OF FORMER MAYOR DING

  Mayor Harrington, on behalf of the City Council and staff, presented former Mayor
  Ding with a gavel plaque commemorating his year of service as mayor.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Joanna Jimenez, representing the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce, presented
  Council Member Ding with a Certificate of Recognition for his service as Mayor.

  Lorena Zavala, representing the Southwest Carpenters' Union, commented on
  construction industry tax fraud .

I  Terri Huerta, Director Of Mission Development for Mission San Gabriel, thanked
  Interim Police Chief Nakamura, Public Works Director/City Engineer de Vinck and their
  staff for the safety provided for the recent Eucharistic Procession.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Member of the public Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nunez requested that Item 4H be pulled
  for separate discussion. Council Member Menchaca requested that Item 4C be pulled
  for separate discussion.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Ding, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4B, and 4D-4G as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  In regard to Item 4C, Council Member Menchaca proposed that Council Member Ding
  be appointed as the delegate, and Council Member Menchaca be appointed as the
  alternate, to the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments. Mayor Harrington
  accepted the proposal. Clarification was made that Council Member Ding would
  continue to serve as the delegate to the Los Angeles Regional Water Quality Control
  Board.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to approve Item 4C as amended.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  April 4, 2023
   Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  In regard to Item 4H, Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nunez commented on the Opioid crisis,
  asked how funds received by the City were used last year and requested that this year's

I  funds be spent on a Narcan distribution and education program.

  Discussion included the Police and Fire Departments' historical, current, and planned
  use of Narcan.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Wu, to
  approve Item 4H as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following :

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular March 7, 2023 Regular Meeting.

I  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular March 21, 2023 Regular Meeting.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved March 10, 2023, and March 17, 2023, Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. MAYOR'S APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES - COUNCIL
  LIAISONS

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-18 confirming the Mayor's
  appointments of Council Members to serve as delegates, alternates and liaisons to
  outside agencies and Committees, as amended to appoint Council Member Ding
  as the delegate, and Council Member Menchaca as the alternate, to the San Gabriel
  Valley Council of Governments.

  D. REQUEST TO APPROVE COMMUNITY PARTNER AGREEMENT IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $8,500 WITH KABOOM!, INCORPORATED FOR COOLIDGE

I  SCHOOL PARK

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to sign the Agreement and act as
  the agent of the City on all matter concerning this project.

  E. GENERAL PLAN HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT FOR THE
  2022 CA LEN DAR YEAR

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  April 4, 2023
   The City Council received and filed the information contained in the staff report
  and directed staff to submit the housing report to the State Department of Housing
  and Community Development.
  F. 2022 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:
  JANUARY 2022 - DECEMBER 2022

  The City Council received and filed the information contained in the staff report
  and directed staff to submit the report to the Office of Planning and Research and
  State Department of Housing and Community Development.

I  G. ADOPTING RESOLUTION NO. 23-12 APPROVING THE SIDE LETTER OF
  AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE MANAGEMENT GROUP

  The City Council:

  1. Adopted Resolution No. 23-12, which approves the Side Letter of Agreement
  amending the standing Memorandum of Understanding between the City and
  Police Management Group; and
  2. Authorized the City's negotiators to execute the Side Letter of Agreement.

  H. NEW NATIONAL OPIOIDS SETTLEMENTS: TEVA, ALLERGAN, CVS,
  WALGREENS, AND WALMART AND STATUS UPDATE REGARDING PREVIOUS
  OPIOID DISTRIBUTOR AND JANSEN SETTLEMENT AGREEMENTS

  The City Council authorized the City Attorney to execute the necessary settlement
  and participation agreements for the new national opioid settlements that have
  been reached with Teva, Allergen, CVS, Walgreens, and Walmart.

I  5. PUBLIC HEARING- None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. DIRECTION ON THE TEMPORARY OUTDOOR BUSINESS PERMIT PROGRAM

  Economic Development Manager Caroline Velarde made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included the proposed guidelines and application process,
  and parking provisions.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included parklet and sidewalk use; continuing the outdoor dining
  permit program versus a Condition-Use Permit (CUP) process; an encroachment
  permit for use of the City right-of-way; desire for flexibility to assist business

I  owners; fee calculation; and temporary-vendor regulations.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to draft a new temporary
  outdoor dining permit program with case- by-case flexibility, including use of the
  public right -of-way.

  B. PUBLIC WORKS ANNUAL UPDATE

  Public Works Director/City Engineer de Vinck made the presentation.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  Ap ril 4, 2023
   There was no public comment.

  Discussion included City and property-owner responsibilities related to trees; 411
  with the Chief participation; collaboration on publicizing Public Works
  accomplishments; great improvement in the City's Pavement Management Index;
  combination of in -house and out-sourced pest control and graffiti abatement;
  fiber-optic camera program for safety and traffic control; Measure R and grant-
  funded projects; required developer-installed new light poles become City
  property that the City must maintain; potential for leasing fiber connectivity to

I  others, status, timeline and functionality of the fiber installation project; repair
  requests from the public; and appreciation for the great job done by Public Works
  Director/City Engineer de Vinck and his staff.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto announced that Congresswoman Chu will be visiting the
  affordable housing site at 405 S. Del Mar on April 11 , 2023, as the site will be included
  in funding received for the Regional Housing Trust.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Wu reported on his attendance at an Upper San Gabriel Municipal Water
  District event related to water conseNation .

  Council Member Chan reported his attendance at the Upper San Gabriel Municipal
  Water District event, a monthly San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce/ Elks meeting, and

I  the Eucharistic walk from Mission San Gabriel to St. Luke's Church in Temple City;
  announced the Annual Kiwanis Club Easter Pancake Breakfast on April 8, 2023, at Smith
  Park; and wished all a Happy Easter.

  Council Member Ding commented on the Kiwanis Club Easter Pancake Breakfast Event
  at which the San Gabriel Hope Lions Club is supporting the coloring contest; reported
  on his visit to a local Chamber of Commerce business, Edible Arrangements, and gave
  a reminder to shop local.

  Council Member Menchaca announced that the Human Equity, Access and Relations
  (HEAR) Commission is looking for youth ambassadors to participate with the
  Commission with an application submission deadline of April 17, 2023, at 4:00 P.M.;
  and announced the Fire Department's three-day Community Emergency Response
  Team (CERT) course and gave contact information.

  At Council Member Menchaca's request, Community Services Manager Matthew
  Morales-Stevens explained that the Easter Pancake Breakfast event is a collaboration
  between the City and private partners, and shared details of the event. Council

I  Member Menchaca provided additional information.

  Mayor Harrington encouraged attendance at the Easter event.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:04 P.M
